statement: The share of NYC new-building jobs that reach a certificate of occupancy within four years of first permit matches the Department of City Planning's statement that 80 to 90 percent of permitted projects are completed within four years.

graph_evidence.summary: Population growth rate and expansion rate of construction land, Chongqing over 20 years (coefficient 1.82; doi:10.1117/12.815931). The only construction-supply finding found in the graph.

Vacant housing demolitions and change in crime, mean difference -0.068 (CI -0.119 to -0.018), PMID 36228876. Shows the graph treats land and buildings as exposures for health and crime, not as supply outcomes.

Variable and concept searches (13 terms, data/derived/construction/graph_search.json) found no finding on building permits, permit-to-completion ratios, lags or permit lapse. The construction concept (COEFxSZVXO) has 3 relationships in all (wage, population growth, natural disasters).

literature.citation: NYC Department of City Planning, 'New Housing Permits in the First Half of 2022' (information brief, 2022)
literature.finding: 'Typically, 80 to 90 percent of permitted projects are completed within four years.' DOB issued permits for about 58,600 homes in the first half of 2022, ahead of the 421-a expiry.

literature.citation: NYU Furman Center, State of New York City's Housing and Neighborhoods / 2019 data on the housing stock
literature.finding: Median time from new-building permit to certificate of occupancy was about 1.9 years for buildings permitted in 2009-2014.

literature.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, New Residential Construction, methodology and 'Relationship between building permits, starts and completions'
literature.finding: Construction is undertaken for all but a very small percentage of units authorized by permit; an older bridge table puts abandonment before start near 1.5% and after start near 0.5%. Counts are housing units, not permit rows.

prediction.magnitude: Registrant's expectation: the job-level share with a first CO (temporary or final) within 4 years of first NB permit, cohorts 2010-2017, is about 0.70, range 0.55 to 0.85; median permit-to-CO time 1.8 to 3.0 years among jobs that reach a CO. Research value: 0.80-0.90 (DCP), median 1.9 years (Furman), near-complete eventual completion (Census).
prediction.support_if: pooled 2010-2017 four-year share between 0.75 and 0.95 (consistent with DCP's 0.80-0.90 given measurement differences)
prediction.refute_if: pooled 2010-2017 four-year share below 0.65 with a 95% interval excluding 0.75; then the NYC job-level data conflict with the DCP statement

plan: Cohort = unique NB job numbers in ipu4-2q9a whose first NB permit (permit_type NB, filing_status INITIAL) was issued 2010-2017. Outcome = earliest CO issue date for the same job number in bs8b-p36w or pkdm-hqz6. Share with CO within 1461 days, by cohort year, with Wilson 95% intervals and pooled. Residential subset checked against DCP Housing Database (br6q-ssj3: datepermit, datecomplt, job_status) as a second measure of the same quantity. Eventual completion share for cohorts 2010-2014 (CO by Nov 2026) compared with the Census near-100% statement.
alternatives: DCP counts projects or units, and units weight large projects that finish more reliably than small one- and two-family jobs
Job numbers change between filing systems (BIS to DOB NOW), so a real CO is not matched
Buildings occupied without a CO (illegal occupancy or only a letter of no objection)
Withdrawn or superseded jobs that never meant to build
